'''MWALI''' (<code>0x36C6921e2CECe9DEc7a5AAC42bC6738011F2a1c9</code>) is the [[Proof of Liquidity|proof-of-liquidity]] token on [[PRANA Blockchain|PRANA]]. It exists to reward and measure the liquidity that backs [[KulaSwap|KULA]]. KULA is the reward token; MWALI is the liquidity token. They are deliberately not the same thing.

== How it is meant to be minted ==

MWALI has exactly one minting role, and it is held by a contract, not a person: the KULA/WPRANA liquidity gauge at <code>0x46d92Ae6F5D55Eb5f12F222e44F0CDAC74E38e45</code>. Liquidity providers to the KULA/WPRANA pair — the Kula-Ring — stake their position in the gauge, and the gauge mints MWALI to them in proportion to the liquidity they supplied and how long they supplied it.

The deployer holds no minting role and has renounced its administrative role. Administration belongs to the DAO timelock, which imposes a two-day delay on changes. The consequence is that '''no human can print MWALI'''.

== Why it is separate from KULA ==

Separating the two lets a liquidity position be counted and governed in its own right rather than existing as a side effect of a reward programme. MWALI can be paired back into KULA, used as governance weight, or wired into further gauges without touching KULA's capped emission schedule. See [[Proof of Liquidity]] for the full argument.

== Current state ==

'''MWALI has never been minted.''' Its total supply is zero.

The cause is a configuration mismatch rather than a flaw in the token: the gauge that holds MWALI's minting role is configured to pay out '''KULA''' instead. Liquidity providers to KULA/WPRANA are therefore receiving the reward token, and the proof-of-liquidity layer is inert. The pool itself is real and supplied — the KULA/WPRANA pair holds meaningful liquidity and is fully staked — so the only missing piece is the gauge's reward-token setting.

Correcting it means repointing the gauge, which is an administrative action behind the two-day timelock.

Until that happens, any description of MWALI as a circulating token would be wrong, and any balance of it would be zero.
